research.summary:
Scope note: the user's broad "stock flips" definition (gaps, breakouts, momentum bursts, reversals, halts, squeezes, insider cluster buys) and the narrower "fast small-cap pump" focus are compatible; this research covers the pump anatomy in depth and supplies numeric signal definitions that also serve the broader detector (insider cluster buys and squeeze inputs included). 

Anatomy (2025-2026): A fast small-cap pump is now two distinct species. (1) The classic intraday "runner": a sub-$20, <10-20M-float Nasdaq/NYSE name with a catalyst (PR, FDA, crypto/AI pivot) gaps pre-market on 5x+ relative volume, spikes in the first 15 minutes (46.6% of highs of day form by 9:45, 85%+ by 10:30 on a 3,200-event Jan 2022-Mar 2026 sample), trips 10% or 20% LULD bands repeatedly ("halt train"), and then fades: 67% close below the open, 72.7% gap down the next day, and runs are frequently capped by a same-day/after-hours 424B5 offering or ATM sales (offering announcements average a 20-30% drop). (2) The "ramp-and-dump" on recent microcap IPOs: Cayman/BVI holdcos with China/HK/SE-Asia operations, $4-$5 IPO price, $5-15M proceeds, boutique underwriters, nominee accounts holding the float; victims recruited via Facebook/Instagram ads into WhatsApp/Telegram "investment clubs" and told when and at what price to buy over weeks or months; then a 50-93% collapse in one or two days. Bloomberg (Jan 29, 2026) found a quarter of the 250+ smallest-tier Nasdaq IPOs since 2023 followed this pattern (~60 firms, ~$16B of market cap destroyed); the FBI logged a 300%+ rise in complaints in 2025; the SEC created a Cross-Border Task Force (Sept 5, 2025) and suspended 15 such issuers between Sept 26, 2025 and June 11, 2026 (QMMM, SDM, EFTY, PLTS, PTNM, EMPG, NUTR, PC, LAWR, MCTA, MAMK, MAGH, JMG, TCGL, HCHL). Examples: QMMM ~$1 to >$300 intraday on a crypto pivot (Sept 9, 2025); MCTA $4 to $29.36 within 10 days of IPO; TCGL $8 to >$300 in two days. 

Regulatory response that changes the universe going forward: IPO proceeds must now fund the entire public float (Mar 2025); minimum public float raised to $15M (effective Jan 2026); $0.10-bid automatic delisting (Jan 2026); no cure period after a reverse split within 1 year or 1:250 cumulative over 2 years (Jan 2025); Nasdaq discretionary denial for manipulation risk (IM-5101-3, Dec 2025) and discretionary delisting after an SEC suspension (IM-5101-4, approved June 3, 2026); $25M minimum IPO for China-based issuers (approved May 14, 2026); $5M MVLS accelerated delisting (approved July 22, 2026 but stayed July 29, 2026 pending Commission review). Expect fewer sub-$15M-float new listings but the existing 2023-2025 cohort remains the hunting ground, and the FINRA 2026 report notes schemes now occur months after IPO rather than at IPO, with the same issuer pumped multiple times. 

For the detector: the early long-side edge is confined to the first 5-15 minutes after the open (or pre-market) on catalyst-backed gappers with no active ATM/shelf and adequate cash; everything else in the dataset says "bag-holder risk," and the recent-IPO ramp profile should be a hard warning flag rather than a long candidate.

signals.name: Pre-market gapper (runner candidate)
signals.definition: Price $1-$20; float <10M (Warrior Trading) or <20M; gap >=10% vs prior close for broad 'flips', >=50% for the pump-fade universe (SmallCapLab) and >=100% for Dux's gap-up short universe; relative volume >=5x 30-day average; pre-market volume >=50k shares by 8:00 ET; a news item (PR/8-K/6-K) in the last 24h. Red flag inside the signal: pre-market volume >50M shares or float rotation >15x (Dux) = exhaustion.
signals.data_needed: Pre-market trades/quotes 4:00-9:30 ET (consolidated feed), float (audited float from Dilution Tracker/Fintel/Finviz), 30-day avg volume, news/PR feed, EDGAR 8-K/6-K.
signals.timing: Pre-market (4:00-9:30 ET); most actionable 8:00-9:30.
signals.source: Warrior Trading '5 pillars' (secondary summaries); Steven Dux small-cap short statistics (tradezella.com/strategies/small-cap-short-strategy); SmallCapLab research (smallcaplab.com/research)

signals.name: Open-spike exhaustion clock (bag-holder timer)
signals.definition: On 50%+ gappers (3,200+ events, Jan 2022-Mar 2026): 46.6% of highs of day are set 9:30-9:45, 85%+ by 10:30; median HOD = +36.1% above open; average LOD = -23.4% below open; 67.2% close below open; 75% close below VWAP; only 3.7% fully round-trip below prior close. Dux: average post-open push 30-35% on 1-2M floats, 20-25% on 5-10M floats, with the best short entries 10:00-11:00. Rule: a long entered after 10:30 on a gapper is trading against a ~70% fade base rate.
signals.data_needed: 1-minute bars, VWAP, open price, HOD/LOD tracking, float bucket.
signals.timing: First 15 minutes (signal window), degrading sharply after 10:30.
signals.source: SmallCapLab research page (unaudited vendor stats); Steven Dux strategy page

signals.name: HOD climax volume vs LOD volume
signals.definition: Median 5-minute volume at the high of day is 2.95M shares (~$10.6M) vs 487K at the low of day (6.1x lower). A 5-minute bar with volume >=3x the prior 5-minute median that fails to make a new high within 5 minutes is a climax/top candidate.
signals.data_needed: 1- or 5-minute volume bars.
signals.timing: During (real time).
signals.source: SmallCapLab research page

signals.name: LULD halt train
signals.definition: Tier 2 NMS stock bands: 10% if prior close >$3.00; 20% if $0.75-$3.00; lesser of $0.15 or 75% if <$0.75 (bands doubled 3:35-4:00 ET for <=$3 names per Nasdaq FAQ). Limit State 15 seconds then 5-minute pause (LUDP); reopen by Nasdaq halt cross with auction collars derived from the triggering band, extended in 5-minute Display Only Periods with collars widened 5%/$0.15 in the imbalance direction; max 10 minutes before other venues may resume. Signal: >=2 LUDP halts within 30 minutes (upward) = strong momentum but not continuation; the most-halted names run 8-9 halts in 30 days. Reference price = 5-minute mean of eligible trades, updated only if >=1% away; bands republished every 30 s.
signals.data_needed: Nasdaq Trader trading-halts page/RSS (reason code LUDP, pause threshold price), SIP LULD band messages, or a halt feed from Benzinga/Trade Ideas/StockTitan.
signals.timing: During; the first halt typically within the opening 5-15 minutes on a runner.
signals.source: Nasdaq LULD FAQ (nasdaqtrader.com/content/MarketRegulation/LULD_FAQ.pdf); SR-NASDAQ-2024-065 (sec.gov 34-101620.pdf) describing Rule 4120(c)(10) collars; thedesperatetrader.com most-halted list

signals.name: News halt reopen collars (T1/T2/T12)
signals.definition: Non-LULD halts (98% news-related in 2023) now reopen through a halt cross with +/-10% collars around the Nasdaq last sale (or prior NOCP), widened by another 10% after a 5-minute display-only period, then 20% per subsequent period (SEC approved Feb 2025). T12 = exchange requested additional information (hours to overnight); H10 = SEC trading suspension (10 business days, exchanges have extended beyond).
signals.data_needed: Halt reason codes from Nasdaq/NYSE halt feeds.
signals.timing: During; T1 can come pre-market on PR; T12 is a late-stage warning.
signals.source: SR-NASDAQ-2024-065 notice (sec.gov) and Federal Register 2025-02386 (Feb 10, 2025); StockTitan halt-code glossary

signals.name: Short-sale restriction (SSR) trigger
signals.definition: Reg SHO Rule 201: when the listing market determines the price fell >=10% from the prior day's regular-session close (last-sale-eligible trades), short sales may only execute above the NBB for the remainder of that day and the next day; can re-trigger daily; applies whenever an NBB is disseminated (including pre-market). For runners, SSR on day 2 after a dump identifies 'backside' names and reduces short pressure, which some traders use for bounce longs.
signals.data_needed: Prior close, intraday low, SIP SSR indicator (or compute).
signals.timing: During (first trigger often in the first hour of a red day) and carries into the next day.
signals.source: SEC Division of Trading and Markets Rule 201 FAQ (sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/rule201faq.htm)

signals.name: Float rotation / dilution capacity (run cap)
signals.definition: Compute cumulative volume / float: >=1x by 10:30 is typical of a runner; >=15x (Dux) marks exhaustion. Combine with Dilution Tracker-style fields: active S-3/F-3 shelf with remaining capacity, open ATM agreement (any 424B5 or 8-K Item 1.01 naming a sales agent), warrants/convertibles with exercise/conversion prices below current price, cash runway <6 months. ATM capacity / market cap >=1x = treat the run as capped. Offering-window heuristic: 40%+ move over 1-5 sessions closing near the high on >=2x 30-day volume = high same-day/after-hours offering probability; 424B5s typically hit EDGAR ~4:05 pm ET and produce a gap-down next open; announcement-day average drop 20-30%.
signals.data_needed: EDGAR full-text/RSS for 424B5, 424B3, S-1, S-3/F-3, 8-K Item 1.01/3.02, 6-K; Dilution Tracker (paid) or own parser; float and shares outstanding.
signals.timing: Pre-market (shelf map) and 4:00-6:00 pm ET (filing watch); same-day registered directs can print intraday.
signals.source: Guy Gentile dilution guide (guygentile.com/articles/guide-to-stock-dilution-tracking); BIT 'ATM dilution trap' (bit.com knowledge hub); Dilution Tracker research as cited by thestockdork.com; Steven Dux strategy page

signals.name: Recent small IPO ramp-and-dump profile (hard warning)
signals.definition: IPO within the last 24 months on Nasdaq Capital Market or NYSE American; IPO price $4-$5; gross proceeds $5-$25M; <20M shares issued; Cayman/BVI holdco with operations in China/HK/Singapore/Malaysia/Indonesia; underwriter in the Bloomberg-named group (WestPark, D. Boral, Dominari, Revere, R.F. Lafferty, Cathay, Bancroft, Prime Number, Benjamin, Joseph Stone); 70-90% of IPO allocation to HK broker-dealers (FINRA 22-25). Behavioral trigger: multi-week grind up (e.g., 2x-5x) on rising volume with no 8-K/6-K/PR, often with layered limit buys above round numbers, followed by a 50%+ drop in 1-2 days. Bloomberg: ~25% of 250+ smallest-tier IPOs since 2023 fit; SEC suspensions came 17 days (PLTS) to months after IPO and generally after the peak.
signals.data_needed: IPO calendar with underwriters/proceeds/jurisdiction (EDGAR F-1/424B4), daily bars, news feed, float concentration.
signals.timing: Weeks before the dump (grind-up phase); dump occurs over 1-2 sessions; SEC suspension is late.
signals.source: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25 (Nov 17, 2022); FINRA 2026 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report, Manipulative Trading; Bloomberg Jan 29, 2026 investigation as quoted in House Financial Services letter (July 1, 2026); Cooley (Apr 28, 2026) and securitieslawyer101 suspension analyses; SEC suspension orders 34-104112/104113

signals.name: No-news parabolic move (manipulation prior)
signals.definition: Close-to-close gain >=100% over <=5 sessions, or >=300% over <=20 sessions, with zero EDGAR filings or PRs in the window, on a sub-$300M microcap. This is the SEC's stated basis language ('recommendations made to investors by unknown persons via social media ... designed to artificially inflate the price and volume') and Atkins' Feb 6, 2026 framing ('no material news ... that would explain the unusual rise').
signals.data_needed: Daily bars, EDGAR filings index, PR wires.
signals.timing: Late in the ramp (days to weeks in); use as a 'do not chase' flag.
signals.source: SEC trading suspension order for QMMM (34-104113); Fox Business interview with Chairman Atkins (Feb 6, 2026)

signals.name: Social-media noise burst
signals.definition: Abnormal post volume >=3 standard deviations vs the ticker's 30-day baseline on StockTwits/X/Reddit plus coordinated identical messaging or new-account clustering; invitations to WhatsApp/Telegram 'investment clubs', 'professor/assistant' personas, screenshot-posting of fills. Academic: +1 unit of noise index = 6-7% higher manipulator profit and ~50% more volume; failed pumps show 14% lower abnormal tweet volume and 29% fewer followers.
signals.data_needed: StockTwits API (free tier), X API (paid), Reddit API, ad-library scraping (optional); NLP classifier (Claude pass).
signals.timing: Pre-market and overnight for runners; weeks ahead for ramp-and-dumps.
signals.source: Cumming & Tran, 'Social Media Noise and Stock Manipulation' (Dec 2025) via Swedroe summary; FBI PSA I-070325 (July 3, 2025); securitieslawyer101 HCHL playbook (July 16, 2026)

signals.name: Pivot PR catalyst (crypto/AI/treasury)
signals.definition: Microcap (<$100M cap) press release announcing a business pivot to crypto treasury, AI, or similar buzzword with no revenue attached. QMMM: ~$1 to >$300 intraday on Sept 9, 2025 (close $207), suspended 20 days later. Treat as a runner catalyst for the first 15 minutes and as a dump setup thereafter.
signals.data_needed: PR wire feed (GlobeNewswire/PRNewswire/ACCESSWIRE), 6-K/8-K.
signals.timing: Pre-market (PR typically 7:00-9:00 ET) or intraday.
signals.source: securitieslawyer101 QMMM/SDM analysis (Sept 30, 2025); SEC order 34-104113

signals.name: Post-reverse-split tiny float
signals.definition: Reverse split effective in the last 30 days (Nasdaq requires 10 calendar days' notice and 2 business days' public disclosure; Nasdaq halts into the effective date and reopens with a halt cross at 9:00 ET under a 2026 rule) producing float <3M shares. Spike-prone on any catalyst because of thin float and borrow scarcity, but academic 20-day post-split CAR is about -19% (worse when controlled), and a split within 1 year (or 1:250 cumulative over 2 years) removes the bid-price cure period, raising delisting risk.
signals.data_needed: Nasdaq corporate-action calendar, 8-K Item 5.03, float after split.
signals.timing: Pre-market on effective date and following weeks.
signals.source: Nasdaq Rule 5250(e)(7) (effective Jan 30, 2025; AFS Law summary); Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv) (SEC approved Jan 2025; reflected in issuer proxy filings); USU graduate report on short selling around reverse splits (not directly fetched; search-level only)

signals.name: Insider cluster buy (microcap)
signals.definition: Form 4 open-market purchase (code P) by an insider when another insider bought within the prior 30 days; filing arrives within 2 business days of the trade. Microcaps ($30M-$500M, 2018-2024, 13,534 purchases): first-day abnormal return 4.4% for clustered vs 2.7% unclustered; 4.13% when the stock is far below its 52-week high vs 0.86% near it; reaction concentrated on day 1 with 2-3 sessions of continuation and no reliable longer drift.
signals.data_needed: EDGAR Form 4 feed (or OpenInsider), 52-week high, market cap.
signals.timing: After-hours/pre-market following the filing; trade the next open.
signals.source: Zhao, 'Insider Purchases Far Below the 52-Week High' (arXiv 2602.06198v2, 2026)

signals.name: Day-2 / first-red-day regime
signals.definition: After a 50%+ gap day: 72.7% gap down next day (median -4.3%), 75.5% open below day-1 open. Dux first-red-day short: >=3 consecutive green days, >=300% range from the breakout (or ~1,000% in 2 days), less than 50% of the move already faded. Long-side multi-day runs are the minority case and usually require fresh news or a squeeze setup.
signals.data_needed: Daily bars, consecutive-green-day counter, breakout reference.
signals.timing: Pre-market of day 2+.
signals.source: SmallCapLab research page; Steven Dux strategy page

signals.name: Squeeze inputs
signals.definition: Short interest >=20% of float (FINRA settlement data, published twice monthly with ~9-day lag), cost-to-borrow >=50% and utilization >=90% (Ortex/Fintel intraday estimates), Reg SHO threshold-list membership (>=0.5% of shares outstanding failing to deliver for 5 consecutive days), float <10M. Note: ramp-and-dump names typically have little real short interest; a 'squeeze' narrative in a WhatsApp group is a pump tell, not a signal.
signals.data_needed: FINRA short interest, exchange threshold lists (daily), SEC FTD files (twice monthly), Ortex/Fintel borrow data.
signals.timing: Pre-market (daily refresh) with intraday borrow updates.
signals.source: Ortex pricing/feature articles (public.ortex.com); Fintel plans page (fintel.io/checkout); FINRA/SEC data descriptions (general knowledge, not fetched)

signals.name: Terminal regulatory events
signals.definition: SEC Section 12(k) suspension (H10 code, 10 business days; the 2025-26 cohort stayed halted for months and Nasdaq can now delist under IM-5101-4); Nasdaq T12 'additional information requested' halt; closing bid <=$0.10 for 10 consecutive days (immediate delisting from Jan 19, 2026); MVLS <$5M for 30 consecutive business days (rule approved July 22, 2026, stayed July 29, 2026).
signals.data_needed: SEC trading-suspensions RSS (sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/trading-suspensions/rss), Nasdaq halt feed, daily close and MVLS.
signals.timing: Late (after the dump) but useful to purge watchlists and block longs.
signals.source: SEC trading suspensions page; Norton Rose Fulbright Nasdaq rule update; Greenberg Traurig (July 2026) and Thomson Reuters (July 29, 2026) on the $5M MVLS rule

facts.claim: Gap-up universe stats (stocks opening >=50% above prior close, min price $0.30, Jan 2022-Mar 2026, 3,200+ events): 67.2% close below open; 46.6% of HODs set 9:30-9:45 and 85%+ by 10:30; median HOD +36.1% from open; average LOD -23.4%; 3.7% full gap fill; 72.7% gap down next day (median -4.3%); fade rate 69.1% for cash-crisis names vs 60.6% for cash-flow-positive; fade rates by gap bucket 69.7% (45-75%), 71.9% (75-100%), 70.5% (100-150%).
facts.source: https://www.smallcaplab.com/research

facts.claim: Dux's small-cap short framework: gap-up shorts on stocks up >100% with initial market cap <$100M, float <50M, price >$3; average post-open push 30-35% on 1-2M floats and 20-25% on 5-10M floats; average risk ~7% vs fade 24-26%; pre-market volume >50M shares or float rotation >15x are warning thresholds; pre-market to full-day volume ratio 1:5 to 1:10.
facts.source: https://www.tradezella.com/strategies/small-cap-short-strategy

facts.claim: Warrior Trading '5 pillars': relative volume >=5x, daily change >=10%, price $1-$20, float <10M, news catalyst; the free TDPro gapper scanner implements float <=10M, >=50k pre-market volume, $1-$20, news within 24h, gap >=10%.
facts.source: https://mcpservers.org/servers/www-traderdaddy-pro-premarket-gappers (secondary); Warrior Trading materials via secondary summaries

facts.claim: LULD bands (Nasdaq FAQ): Tier 2 prior close >$3.00 = 10% all day; $0.75-$3.00 = 20% (doubled to 40% 3:35-4:00 pm); <$0.75 = lesser of $0.15 or 75%; Limit State lasts 15 seconds then a 5-minute pause; reference price is the 5-minute arithmetic mean of eligible trades, updated only if >=1% away, republished every 30 seconds; max pause 10 minutes after which other venues may resume; reopening price becomes the new reference if reopened within 10 minutes.
facts.source: https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/MarketRegulation/LULD_FAQ.pdf

facts.claim: Nasdaq reopens LULD pauses via its halt cross with initial auction collars based on the triggering price band (since 2017), extending in 5-minute Display Only Periods with collars widened in the imbalance direction; the collar threshold for LULD/MWCB is 5% of the auction reference price with a $0.15 minimum. For news and other non-LULD halts (98% news-related in 2023), SR-NASDAQ-2024-065 added symmetric 10% collars (greater of $1 or 10% above $1; $0.50 or 10% at <=$1), widened by 10% after the first extension and 20% thereafter until the price falls within collars; SEC approved Feb 2025.
facts.source: https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2024/34-101620.pdf; https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/02/10/2025-02386

facts.claim: Reg SHO Rule 201: short-sale price test activates when the listing market determines a >=10% decline from the prior day's regular-session close (last-sale-eligible trades 9:30-4:00), lasts the remainder of the day and the next day, can re-trigger without limit, and applies whenever an NBB is disseminated including outside regular hours.
facts.source: https://www.sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/rule201faq.htm

facts.claim: SR-NASDAQ-2024-084 (SEC accelerated approval March 12, 2025): a company listing via IPO must satisfy the minimum Market Value of Unrestricted Publicly Held Shares solely from offering proceeds; previously registered resale shares no longer count. Minimums at the time: Capital Market $5M (net income standard) / $15M (equity or MVLS standards); Global Market $8M / $18M / $20M.
facts.source: https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2025/34-102622.pdf; https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/assets/rulebook/nasdaq/filings/SR-NASDAQ-2024-084.pdf

facts.claim: Nasdaq's Sept 3, 2025 proposal raised MVUPHS under the net income standard to $15M (Capital Market from $5M; Global Market from $8M), required China-based IPOs to raise >=$25M gross, and proposed accelerated delisting for companies with MVLS <$5M (10 consecutive business days in the proposal) plus another deficiency, citing 'concerns about manipulative practices, including pump-and-dump schemes, in smaller company securities.' SEC approved the $15M float rule Dec 18, 2025; operative Jan 16-17, 2026.
facts.source: https://acrosstheboard.mayerbrown.com/2025/09/nasdaq-rule-proposal-seeks-enhanced-float-and-ipo-listing-requirements-faster-delisting-for-non-compliant-companies/; https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/3fe61375/nasdaq-rule-update

facts.claim: Low-price rule: SEC approved Dec 5, 2025, operative Jan 19, 2026: a closing bid of $0.10 or less for 10 consecutive trading days triggers an immediate delisting determination with no cure period and immediate trading suspension.
facts.source: https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/3fe61375/nasdaq-rule-update

facts.claim: Reverse-split rules: Nasdaq Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv) (SEC approved Jan 2025) denies any bid-price compliance period if the company effected a reverse split in the prior one year or splits totaling >=1:250 in the prior two years; Rule 5250(e)(7) (from Jan 30, 2025) requires notice to Nasdaq 10 calendar days before the split's market effective date and public disclosure 2 business days before; a 2026 filing (34-105860) has Nasdaq halting the security before the effective date and reopening via halt cross at 9:00 am ET.
facts.source: https://www.afslaw.com/perspectives/alerts/nasdaq-rule-change-lengthens-reverse-stock-split-notice-period; https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105860.pdf; Nasdaq issuer proxy disclosures (e.g., Reviva PRE 14A, Oct 2025)

facts.claim: Nasdaq IM-5101-3 (effective Dec 19, 2025) lets Nasdaq deny initial listings whose securities are 'susceptible to manipulation', considering jurisdiction/remedies, concentration of public float and underwriter allocations, advisors' involvement in prior offerings with 'concerning or volatile trading patterns', FINRA/SEC referrals, and going-concern opinions; it was framed as a response to SEC suspensions based on social-media-driven manipulation without issuer misconduct.
facts.source: https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/01/nasdaq-expands-discretionary-authority-to-deny-initial-listings-based-on-manipulation-risk

facts.claim: Nasdaq IM-5101-4 (filed Feb 20, 2026; SEC accelerated approval June 3, 2026) authorizes Nasdaq to delist a security after an SEC trading suspension even if the issuer meets all listing standards and had no connection to the trading, considering float, trading patterns, jurisdiction, recent capital raises/resale dynamics, disclosure adequacy, and advisors' regulatory history.
facts.source: https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/assets/rulebook/nasdaq/filings/SR-NASDAQ-2026-009.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/file/34-105603

facts.claim: SEC approved Nasdaq's $25M minimum firm-commitment IPO proceeds requirement for China-based (incl. Hong Kong and Macau) companies on May 14, 2026, operative mid-June 2026; Nasdaq's filing stated that from Aug 2022 to Apr 2025 about 70% of its market-manipulation enforcement referrals involved Chinese companies although they are under 10% of Nasdaq listings.
facts.source: https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2026/5/sec-approves-nasdaqs-25-million-ipo-requirement-for-china-based-companies

facts.claim: The $5M MVLS continued-listing rule (SR-NASDAQ-2026-004: MVLS <$5M for 30 consecutive business days = immediate suspension and delisting, no cure, hearing request does not stay suspension) was approved July 22, 2026 and effective July 23, 2026, then stayed by the Commission on July 29, 2026 pending review after five petitions; roughly 100-200 listed companies are below $5M and SEC analysis found 983 companies would have triggered it 2006-2025.
facts.source: https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2026/7/sec-approves-nasdaqs-new-$5-million-mvls-continued-listing-standard; https://tax.thomsonreuters.com/news/sec-stays-controversial-nasdaq-5-million-listing-rule-pending-review/

facts.claim: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25 (Nov 17, 2022) profiled small-cap IPO ramp-and-dumps: raises under $25M, issuers valued under $100M, fewer than 20M shares issued, many China-based, Hong Kong broker-dealers allocated up to 90% of shares; price spikes in the opening trade and in the day(s) after listing with no news, then declines to at or below the IPO price; nominee accounts place layered buy limit orders above the IPO price at the same time.
facts.source: https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/22-25

facts.claim: FINRA's 2026 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report says suspected pump-and-dumps now occur less often at the IPO and more often months after it, the same issuer can be pumped multiple times, nominee accounts transfer shares to foreign omnibus accounts to concentrate float, issuers do large privately placed secondaries to select foreign investors, account-takeover fraud is used to buy targeted stocks, and 'investment clubs' direct victims on the time and price to buy while foreign-controlled accounts sell.
facts.source: https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/guidance/reports/2026-finra-annual-regulatory-oversight-report/manipulative-trading

facts.claim: FBI PSA I-070325 (July 3, 2025): ramp-and-dump operators use social-media ads to recruit into 'investment clubs' on messaging apps (with bots/fake members), secretly control a large block of a low-priced stock, ramp it over 'several weeks or months', then dump; the FBI saw at least a 300% increase in such complaints in 2025 vs 2024.
facts.source: https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250703

recommendations: Treat the detector as two separate classifiers: (A) 'runner' (intraday catalyst-driven gapper) where the only long edge is pre-market to ~9:45 ET and everything after 10:30 is short/fade territory by base rate; (B) 'ramp-and-dump' (recent microcap IPO, grind-up without news) which should never emit a long alert and should emit a 'do not touch / bag-holder' alert once the grind-up exceeds ~100% over 20 sessions with no filings.

Cheap rules pass for A (all free data): price $1-$20, float <20M (hard cap) with <10M preferred, pre-market gap >=10% (broad) / >=50% (pump universe), pre-market volume >=50k by 8:00 ET and relative volume >=5x, a news item or 8-K/6-K within 24h, and no 424B5/S-1/S-3 filed in the last 5 sessions. Score down: float rotation >1x pre-market, pre-market volume >50M shares, prior-day run already >=300% from breakout, cash runway <6 months or active ATM/shelf (DilutionTracker or own EDGAR parser), reverse split in last 30 days.

Cheap rules pass for B: IPO within 24 months on Nasdaq Capital Market/NYSE American, IPO price $4-$5, proceeds <=$25M, foreign (Cayman/BVI) holdco with China/HK/SE-Asia operations, underwriter in the Bloomberg-named list, float <20M; then watch for 5-day gain >=50% or 20-day gain >=100% with zero EDGAR filings. Send Claude only the survivors with the news/filing context so it can judge 'is there a real catalyst' (the SEC's own test).

Instrument the halt and SSR state machine directly: subscribe to Nasdaq Trader's halt RSS (or a Polygon/Databento-style halt/LULD feed), compute band width from the prior close ($3.00 and $0.75 thresholds), count LUDP halts per 30 minutes, and compute SSR from the prior close; 2+ up-halts inside 30 minutes plus float rotation >=1x is the 'climax zone' in the data, not a buy signal.

Add a 4:00-6:00 pm ET EDGAR watcher for 424B5/424B3/8-K Item 1.01 and 3.02/6-K on every name that ran >=40% in the last 1-5 sessions; an offering print should cancel any day-2 long thesis and generate a 'gap-down expected' alert (announcement-day average drop 20-30%).

Add Form 4 cluster-buy detection for the broad 'flips' interpretation: purchases (code P) by >=2 insiders within 30 days on a $30M-$500M name far below its 52-week high, alert on the filing evening and expect a day-1 reaction of a few percent with 2-3 days of follow-through; keep position expectations small.

For squeeze setups, pay for one borrow-data source (Ortex Advanced $129/month or Fintel) rather than relying on twice-monthly FINRA data, and discount any 'squeeze' narrative on a name that fits the ramp-and-dump profile.

Data/tool budget guidance: a free-first stack (EDGAR full-text + RSS, Nasdaq halt RSS, SEC suspensions RSS, StockTwits API, Finviz Elite $39.50 for screens) plus one of Dilution Tracker ($49-74/month) and one halt/scanner feed (Benzinga Pro Streamlined $147 if squawk is wanted, otherwise a market-data API) covers everything in the lifecycle; Trade Ideas is only worth $89-254/month if you want its halt/gap scanners instead of writing your own.

Maintain a 'tainted issuer' blocklist seeded from SEC 12(k) suspensions (15 since Sept 2025), Nasdaq T12 halts, and the Bloomberg underwriter list; and expect the listed universe of sub-$15M-float names to shrink after the Jan 2026 float rule, the May 2026 $25M China rule, and the stayed $5M MVLS rule.

Backtest the long-side rules against the SmallCapLab-style base rates before trusting them: with ~70% of 50%+ gappers closing below the open and 73% gapping down next day, the detector's success metric should be time-to-alert relative to the 9:30-9:45 HOD window, not hit rate on 'runs'.

research.summary: Yes, both layers can be built on the same feeds: the broad "stock flips" layer (gaps, breakouts, halts, reversals, squeezes, insider cluster buys) and this narrower small-cap runner/pump layer, which is a specialization of it with tighter universe filters (price $1-20, float <20M, market cap <$100-200M) and a dedicated "dump" rule set. Research on the narrow layer: the practitioner consensus for the LONG early phase is Ross Cameron's "five pillars" (RVOL >=5x vs 30-day average, already up >=10% on the day, a headline catalyst, price $1.00-$20.00, float under 20M shares; gaps scanned from 4%, 20%+ preferred; entry on the pre-market-high break or 1-minute opening-range breakout with the stop at that candle's low, only above VWAP, between roughly 7:00 and 11:00 ET). The AVOID/SHORT side is better quantified than the long side: Steven Dux's gap-up short needs the stock up >100%, float <50M, market cap <$100M, price >$3, and confirmation that price is below the open by ~10:00 with declining volume (holding above the open at 10:00 invalidates); first red day needs >=3 consecutive green days and ~300% range (or ~1,000% in 2 days) and is skipped if the red day already gave back >50% of the run; Investors Underground says never short the frontside (big candles, rising volume) and wait for the backside (fading volume, failed red-to-green recoveries, VWAP loss); multi-halt exhaustion shorts start after 4-5 up-halts; float rotation >5x pre-market means positioning is unknowable and >15x is a no-trade. Dilution/offering signals are the most mechanical dump predictor: S-3 shelf/ATM prospectus supplement, S-1 resale, 8-K securities purchase agreement with warrant coverage, 424B pricing, going-concern language, cash runway <2 quarters; EDGAR posts filings publicly ~40 seconds (median 36 s) after acceptance. Regulator data on promoted stocks: FINRA 22-25 ramp-and-dump IPOs raised <$25M, issued <20M shares, were valued <$100M, had 90%+ allocations to Hong Kong brokers, and ran on no news; FINRA/SEC 2025 alerts and the SEC Cross-Border Task Force (Sept 5 2025) focus on WhatsApp/Telegram group pumps of Nasdaq-listed China-linked small caps (some +2,000% to +32,000% then collapse). Academic baselines: spam-touted stocks earn +4.9% the day before/of touting and lose ~5.25% over the next two days; abnormal Twitter message volume on small caps precedes an event-day spike and a reversal within the following week; a crypto-derived anomaly detector flags a pump when volume is +300% and price +5% versus a trailing window (balanced) or +400%/+10% (strict). Data-wise, Alpaca Algo Trader Plus ($99/mo, SIP) covers pre-market trades/quotes, trading-status (halt) and LULD channels, a Benzinga news websocket, and SIP-based most-actives/movers screeners; Massive needs the $199/mo Advanced plan for real-time trades/quotes and LULD; none of Alpaca, Massive or Finnhub supplies float, so float must come from FMP/sec-api/dilution-tracker-type vendors or be derived from EDGAR cover pages. LULD does not operate pre-market, so pre-market "halts" are news halts (T1) only; Tier 2 bands are 10% above $3 and 20% between $0.75-$3, with a 15-second limit state and 5-minute pause.

signals.name: LONG: Gap-and-go / five-pillars composite (Ross Cameron, Warrior Trading)
signals.definition: Pre-market gap up (scanners start at 4%; 5%+ acceptable, 20%+ preferred); relative volume >= 5x the 30-day average volume (Class 3 course floor was 2x); already up >= 10% on the day; a news headline that justifies the move (or a former runner / daily-chart breakout); price $1.00-$20.00 (sweet spot $2-$10; small-account variant $5-$10); float under 20M preferred, under 10M ideal, 'under 20mil in hot market, under 10mil in cold market', rarely over 100M. Candidate must be 'Top 5 on Gap Scanner' with a positive catalyst.
signals.data_needed: Pre-market trades (SIP, 4:00-9:30 ET) for gap % and pre-market volume; 30-day average daily volume; float; real-time news headlines keyed by ticker; prior daily bars for 'former runner' flag.
signals.timing: pre-market (watchlist built 7:00-9:30 ET); confirmation at 9:30-9:45
signals.source: Warrior Trading 2025 Small Account Tool Kit PDF (cdn.warriortrading.com/.../2025-Small-Account-Tool-Kit-1013.pdf) and Day Trading Course Class 3 Stock Selection PDF (media.warriortrading.com/2014/09/WarriorTrading-DayTradingCourse-Class3.pdf); warriortrading.com/gap-go/

signals.name: LONG: Pre-market-high break / 1-minute opening range breakout
signals.definition: Mark the pre-market high; buy the break of the pre-market high or the 1-minute opening-range breakout with the stop at the low of that candle; 'volume spiking at or around time of entry' is required; trade window 7:00-11:00 ET; exits on MACD cross, decreasing volume, or 'jackknife rejection'. Only applied to leading gappers / leading RVOL names, not to any stock.
signals.data_needed: 1-minute bars including pre-market; per-bar volume; real-time trades to detect the break.
signals.timing: first 5 min (9:30-9:35) and the first hour
signals.source: warriortrading.com/gap-go/ (search snippet), Warrior 2025 toolkit PDF

signals.name: LONG filter / SHORT invalidation: VWAP relationship
signals.definition: Above VWAP = strong, below VWAP = weak (Investors Underground). Longs only above VWAP. A gap-up that reclaims VWAP and holds is a gap-and-go, not a fade; the short thesis is invalidated on a VWAP reclaim. The '9:45 VWAP rejection' short waits for the gap to fade to VWAP, test it from below and fail, entered ~9:45 after the chaotic first 15 minutes.
signals.data_needed: Trades with size to compute session VWAP (decide whether to include pre-market volume); 1-minute bars.
signals.source: investorsunderground.com/short-selling-stocks/; curvedtrading.com 9:45 VWAP rejection article

signals.name: LONG momentum / SHORT caution: Float rotation
signals.definition: Float rotation = cumulative volume / float. 0.5x = interest building, 1x = full rotation, 2x+ very high volatility, 3x+ rare. >1x already pre-market = squeeze fuel (late shorts can't know who is trapped). Pre-market rotation of ~5x (ICCM: 15M shares vs 2.81M post-reverse-split float) = do not short; Dux reduces or avoids above ~15x. For late long entries above 2x, only buy clear pullbacks with tight stops.
signals.data_needed: Accurate float (refresh after offerings/reverse splits); cumulative volume including pre-market.
signals.timing: pre-market and continuously during
signals.source: curvedtrading.com ICCM float-rotation article; tradezella.com/strategies/small-cap-short-strategy (Dux); TradingView Float Rotation Tracker; investorsunderground.com/short-selling-stocks/

signals.name: LONG momentum / SHORT exhaustion: LULD up-halt ladder
signals.definition: Tier 2 (most small caps): band 10% above $3, 20% for $0.75-$3, lesser of $0.15 or 75% under $0.75; bands doubled in the last 25 minutes for Tier 1 and Tier 2 under $3; 15-second limit state then 5-minute pause (extendable 5 more). Consecutive up-halts ('squeeze, halt, squeeze, halt') mark a live runner; Dux-style exhaustion shorts are only considered after 4-5 up-halts. LULD does not apply pre-market, so any pre-market halt is a news halt (T1), not volatility. Reliability is strong for detecting the halt itself but only moderate as a direction signal.
signals.data_needed: LULD band/halt/resume stream (Alpaca 'lulds' + 'statuses' channels; Massive LULD channel indicators 17 = halt, 18 = resume, Nasdaq-listed only) or Nasdaq trade-halts RSS (1-minute TTL).
signals.timing: during (9:30-16:00 only)
signals.source: luldplan.com; massive.com/blog/luld-massive-websockets; docs.alpaca.markets real-time stock data; nasdaqtrader.com/rss.aspx?feed=tradehalts; Warrior Class 3 PDF; tradezella shorting-strategy page

signals.name: LONG: First green day / red-to-green (Sykes, Grittani)
signals.definition: After a multi-day run and sell-off, the first day the stock closes green with 'minimal selling, lots of buying, and shorts covering'; intraday red-to-green = price crossing above the prior day's close after opening below it (bearish mirror: green-to-red). Grittani-associated overnight pattern: buy the first green day bounce, sell the next-morning gap.
signals.data_needed: Daily bars, prior close, intraday price vs prior close.
signals.timing: during (R2G) or late day (first green close)
signals.source: timothysykes.com/blog/trading-patterns/ and /first-green-day-pattern/; bullishbears.com red-to-green; Grittani attribution via chatwithtraders/tradezella (secondary, unverified)

signals.name: LONG (reversal): Panic dip buy (Sykes)
signals.definition: At least a 20-30% drop in minutes on heavy selling in a former runner, bought as the flush ends; Dux's bounce-short mirror requires prior-day trapped volume >= 2:1 vs current buying.
signals.data_needed: 1-minute bars with volume; prior-day volume-at-price for the trapped-volume ratio.
signals.timing: during
signals.source: timothysykes.com/blog/trading-patterns/; tradezella small-cap-short-strategy (Dux)

signals.name: LONG (swing): Short-squeeze structure
signals.definition: Short interest >= 25% of float (over 50% structurally fragile), days-to-cover >= 5 (7-15 high, 15+ extreme), low float, plus a catalyst; needs 3-4 of the 5 components, not one. FINRA short interest is only settlement-date 15th and month-end, published 7 business days later, so it is stale for same-day pumps; use daily Reg SHO short-volume files as a proxy. Moderate as a structural screen, weak for timing.
signals.data_needed: FINRA equity short interest (bi-monthly), FINRA Reg SHO daily short-sale volume files, float.
signals.timing: pre-market (static screen)
signals.source: curvedtrading.com how-to-find-short-squeeze-stocks; finra.org equity short interest and short-sale-volume pages

signals.name: LONG/AVOID gate: News catalyst present
signals.definition: Breaking headline that 'justifies why the stock is moving' (earnings, FDA, contract, partnership; an offering is NOT a positive catalyst). Stocks up on no news 'carry more risk of a sudden drop'; FINRA's key ramp-and-dump indicator is a price increase 'that did not appear to be driven by news or material events'. Warrior uses Benzinga squawk; Tim Bohen's news filter uses ~5,000 shares pre-market / 1M shares late-day minimum volume.
signals.data_needed: Real-time ticker-tagged news stream (Alpaca v1beta1/news websocket from Benzinga; Massive/Finnhub news REST), EDGAR 8-K stream.
signals.timing: pre-market and continuous
signals.source: Warrior 2025 toolkit PDF; FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25; stockstotrade.com Bohen pages

signals.name: AVOID/SHORT: Gap-up short / 'gap and crap' (Steven Dux)
signals.definition: Universe: market cap under $100M (up to ~$200M for first red day), float below 50M (1-2M very low, 2-5M mid, 5-10M larger), price above $3, excluding biotech, energy and thin Chinese tickers. Setup: stock up more than 100%; average post-open push 30-35% for 1-2M floats and 20-25% for 5-10M floats, then first weakness 10:00-11:00 after ~1 hour consolidation. Confirmation: trading below the open price by ~10:00 with declining volume; holding above the open at 10:00 = weak setup. Smaller gaps (20-40%) avoided. Avoid if >50M shares traded pre-market or float rotated >15x. Average risk ~7%, fade ~24-26%, R:R ~1:3.5-1:4. Day volume estimated at 5-10x pre-market volume.
signals.data_needed: Pre-market volume, open price, 1-minute bars, float, market cap, sector.
signals.timing: first 5 min to 10:00-11:00 ET
signals.source: tradezella.com/strategies/small-cap-short-strategy and /shorting-strategy (secondary summaries of Dux's course; numbers unverified against Dux directly)

signals.name: AVOID/SHORT: First red day (Sykes, Grittani, Dux)
signals.definition: Multi-day runner (200%-500%+ in a few days) closes below the prior close for the first time. Dux quantification: at least 3 consecutive green days and roughly 300% range (2-day exception needs ~1,000%); a red or flat day resets the count; skip if the red day already erased >50% of the run; enter on confirmation (break of prior close or failed retest of resistance), often the following day if it opens weak; high-volume red candle = high conviction, low-volume red = weak.
signals.data_needed: Daily bars (consecutive green count, cumulative range), prior close, intraday volume.
signals.timing: late (first red close) and next-day pre-market gap
signals.source: timothysykes.com/blog/first-red-day-pattern-trading/; tradezella small-cap-short-strategy; tradezero.com first-red-day blog

signals.name: AVOID/SHORT: Frontside vs backside of a parabolic move (Nathan Michaud / Investors Underground)
signals.definition: Frontside = high volume, large candles, still making highs: do not short ('avoid like the plague'). Backside = volume fades, hype dies, stock makes a few failed recovery attempts (red-to-green attempts that fail) then fizzles back to the breakout point; short with defined risk against the last lower high. Checklist also includes crowded-short risk, float rotation, VWAP strength, borrow availability.
signals.data_needed: 1/5-minute bars, volume trend, VWAP, lower-high detection.
signals.timing: during (after the peak) and the following days
signals.source: investorsunderground.com/short-selling-stocks/ and learn-short-selling-day-trading-guide/

signals.name: AVOID/SHORT: Offering filed / dilution ability
signals.definition: Filings that predict the dump: S-3 shelf (baby-shelf rule: issuers with public float under $75M may sell at most one-third of float per 12 months), ATM prospectus supplement or 'equity distribution agreement', S-1 resale registration and its notice of effectiveness, 8-K securities purchase agreement (share count, price, warrant coverage), 424B pricing/reset/ratchet terms, 'substantial doubt ... going concern', 'we will need to raise additional capital'. Heuristics: cash runway < 2 quarters = likely issuer; shelf capacity vs market cap; reverse split + new registration. Offerings are typically priced at a discount into the spike, so a filing during or right after a runner is the single strongest 'bag holder' warning.
signals.data_needed: Real-time EDGAR stream filtered by CIK for forms S-1, S-3, 424B*, 8-K (items 1.01, 3.02, 8.01), 6-K for foreign issuers; latest 10-Q/10-K cash and burn; warrant tables.
signals.timing: pre-market or after close (filings accepted 6:00-22:00 ET; after 17:30 ET they carry the next business day's date)
signals.source: curvedtrading.com how-to-spot-dilution-sec-filings and ATM/S-3 guide; Chicago Booth 'Run EDGAR Run' latency study (40 s mean, 36 s median posting delay)

signals.name: AVOID: Promoted-stock / ramp-and-dump profile (FINRA, SEC)
signals.definition: Recent small-cap IPO that raised < $25M, issued < 20M shares, valued < $100M, with 90%+ of allocations to foreign (mostly Hong Kong) brokers; price rises sharply on IPO day or days after with no news, then falls to or below the offering price. 2024-25 variant: Nasdaq-listed China-linked small caps pumped in WhatsApp/Telegram groups recruited via social ads, some rising 2,000%-32,000% before collapsing; Nasdaq's Sept 3 2025 proposals require $15M minimum unrestricted public float for new listings and $25M proceeds for China-based issuers plus faster delisting below $5M market value; SEC Cross-Border Task Force formed Sept 5 2025.
signals.data_needed: IPO date and proceeds (S-1/424B4), shares offered, country of operations (from filings), social-chat mention counts if scraped, absence of news.
signals.timing: pre-market (static profile) with intraday no-news spike as trigger
signals.source: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25; finra.org ramp-and-dump insights; Nasdaq rule proposals (Mayer Brown / Mondaq summaries, Sept 2025); SEC Cross-Border Task Force press coverage (Ropes & Gray, White & Case)

signals.name: AVOID: Social/spam tout anomaly
signals.definition: Abnormally high social message count about a small cap is associated with a large event-day price increase followed by a sharp reversal over the next trading week (Renault 2017). Email spam touts: buying the day before heavy touting and selling the morning after earned +4.9%; buying on the heaviest-tout day lost ~5.25% over the next two days (Frieder & Zittrain). Detection template from crypto (Kamps & Kleinberg): flag when volume > trailing-window average by 300% and price by 5% ('balanced', 12-hour window) or 400% and 10% ('strict', 24-hour window) - adapt the window to 1-5 minute equity bars.
signals.data_needed: Social mention counts (StockTwits/X/Reddit scrape), OTC Markets Promotion Data (OTC only), StockPromoters.com style promoter DB, 1-minute bars for the anomaly test.
signals.timing: pre-market (tout detection) and first 5 min (anomaly trigger)
signals.source: Renault (2017) 'Market manipulation and suspicious stock recommendations on social media'; Frieder & Zittrain (2007) 'Spam Works'; Kamps & Kleinberg (2018) Crime Science; otcmarkets.com promotion data

signals.name: AVOID/SHORT context: SSR (Rule 201) trigger
signals.definition: A decline of 10% or more from the prior close triggers the alternative uptick rule for the rest of that day and the next day: short sales only above the national best bid. Routinely tripped by small-cap movers; marks that the dump has started and changes short execution. Mechanical, so strong as a detection; it is context, not a directional edge.
signals.data_needed: Prior close and real-time last price; many feeds expose an SSR flag in status messages.
signals.timing: during
signals.source: SEC Rule 201 press release 2010-26; curvedtrading.com SSR explainer

signals.name: AVOID (catastrophic): Regulatory halt codes T1/T2/T12/H10
signals.definition: T1 = news pending, no fixed duration; T2 = news released, typically ~1 hour; T12 = additional information requested by Nasdaq, can last days to weeks and often precedes delisting; H10 = SEC trading suspension up to 10 days; LUDP = 5-minute volatility pause. T12 and H10 on a runner mean the long cannot exit and the reopening is usually far lower.
signals.data_needed: Nasdaq trade-halts RSS (fields: symbol, halt time, reason code, resumption quote/trade time; TTL 1 minute) or Alpaca 'statuses' channel (sc/sm/rc/rm fields).
signals.timing: any time including pre-market
signals.source: nasdaqtrader.com/rss.aspx?feed=tradehalts (fetched); bullishbears.com / CFI halt-code explainers

signals.name: Secondary (broad layer only): Insider cluster buys
signals.definition: Multiple insiders filing Form 4 open-market purchases within a short window; not a small-cap runner signal and not covered by the pump-detection sources above - keep it in the broad 'flips' layer with its own EDGAR Form 4 filter. Weak for day-trading timing because Form 4s are filed up to 2 business days after the trade.
signals.data_needed: EDGAR Form 4 stream (transaction code P, non-derivative).
signals.timing: late (filed within 2 business days of trade)
signals.source: Not researched in this pass (marked unverified)

He targets stocks that can gain 20-30% and cites 50-100%+ intraday moves from supply/demand imbalance.

Scanners run in Trade-Ideas scanning for 4% gaps and earnings, built from 'HIGH Pre-Market Volume'; watchlist example '$GBSN 3.9mil share float, gapping up 7.5%'.

facts.claim: Tim Sykes first red day: find a multi-day runner up 200% to 500% over a few days, short near the retest of resistance, stop just above resistance, cover near support. Panic dip buy requires at least a 20-30% drop in minutes.
facts.source: https://www.timothysykes.com/blog/first-red-day-pattern-trading/ and https://www.timothysykes.com/blog/trading-patterns/

facts.claim: Steven Dux filters (as summarized by TradeZella): market cap under $100M (first red day up to ~$200M), float below 50M, price above $3, exclude biotech/energy/thin Chinese tickers; gap-up short requires up >100%; avoid if >50M shares traded pre-market or float rotated >15x; first red day requires >=3 green days and ~300% range (or ~1,000% in 2 days), skip if >50% of run already erased; bounce short needs trapped-volume ratio >= 2:1; position caps ~10% of float and ~1% of volume; day volume ~5-10x pre-market volume; multi-halt short after 4-5 up-halts; institutional ownership preferred under ~40%.

facts.source: NBER w24083; Harvard DASH 'Spam Works'; EFMA 2017 Renault paper; Crime Science 2018 s40163-018-0093-5; arXiv 2105.00733

facts.source: SEC press release 2010-26; curvedtrading SSR explainer

recommendations: Build the narrow layer as a filter chain on the broad layer: universe gate (price $1-$20, float <20M, market cap <$200M, not an ETF/SPAC), then the five-pillars rules pass (RVOL >=5x vs 30-day ADV computed on cumulative volume including pre-market, gap >=4% with 20%+ as 'A' grade, day change >=10%, catalyst headline present within 24h), then Claude classification only on survivors that also show a pre-market-high break or 1-min ORB above VWAP. Expect a handful of names per day, which keeps the Claude cost small.

Run a separate 'bag holder' scorer that can fire on the same ticker at any time: +3 if any S-1/S-3/424B/8-K item 3.02 or 'equity distribution agreement' filing by the issuer's CIK in the last 10 days or during the run; +2 if cash runway <2 quarters or going-concern language in the last 10-Q/10-K; +2 if float rotation >5x pre-market; +2 if price below the 9:30 open at 10:00 with falling 1-min volume (Dux gap-and-crap confirmation); +2 if VWAP lost and not reclaimed by 9:45-10:00; +2 if 4+ up-halts today; +3 if first red day after >=3 green days / ~300% run; +3 if IPO <12 months ago with proceeds <$25M, <20M shares offered, China/HK operations, or move on no news (FINRA profile); +1 if SSR triggered. Alert as 'DO NOT HOLD / short watch' above a threshold you calibrate on logged runners.

Data stack for a solo developer: Alpaca Algo Trader Plus ($99/mo) gives SIP pre-market trades and quotes from 4:00 ET, the statuses and lulds channels, the Benzinga news websocket and SIP-based most-actives/movers screeners in one subscription; use the free IEX tier only for prototyping because it misses most pre-market prints. Massive Advanced ($199/mo) is the alternative if you want its LULD channel and flat files, but note its halt indicators cover Nasdaq-listed tickers only. Poll the free Nasdaq trade-halts RSS every 60 s as a cross-check for T1/T2/T12/H10 codes, which the LULD channel does not label.

Source float separately and refresh it daily plus on any 8-K/424B/reverse-split event: FMP shares-float or sec-api outstanding-shares endpoints for the baseline, Massive/Finnhub shares outstanding as a sanity check, and a dilution vendor (AskEdgar Dilution Risk Monitor or Dilutracker) if you want warrants, ATM capacity and cash runway precomputed. Treat float as stale by default; a mismatch between shares outstanding and vendor float on a runner is itself a flag.

Subscribe to a push EDGAR stream (sec-api.io websocket or an SSE equivalent) filtered to the tickers currently on your runner list plus form types S-1, S-3, S-3ASR, 424B3/424B4/424B5, 8-K, 6-K, F-1, F-3, and route any hit on an active runner straight to the alert path without waiting for the rules pass; the 40-second EDGAR posting delay means a 'filing while halted' alert can still beat the reopen.

Calibrate the undocumented numbers empirically before trusting them: log every pre-market gapper meeting the universe gate for 30-60 days with pre-market volume at 8:00/9:00/9:25, first-5-minute volume, float rotation, halt count, VWAP status at 9:45 and 10:00, and the eventual high-of-day time and close-vs-open; then fit the first-5-minute volume threshold and the ORB success rate yourself rather than taking any vendor's figure. Keep the Dux and Warrior numbers as priors, not ground truth.

For promo/pump detection, do not try to scrape WhatsApp; instead combine (a) the FINRA structural profile from filings (small recent IPO, HK/China operations, tiny float), (b) a no-news spike test (price +10% and volume +300-400% vs trailing window with no Benzinga/EDGAR item in 24h), and (c) StockTwits/X mention-count anomalies if you already ingest them. Alert these as 'promoted - no long' regardless of the momentum score.

Add halt semantics to the classifier prompt: LUDP = momentum (count them), T1 pre-market = news pending (wait for the headline before any long), T12 or H10 = exit/no-trade and mark the ticker toxic for the session. Also tell Claude whether LULD is even active (it is not before 9:30), so it does not infer a 'halt' from a pre-market gap in prints.
