research.summary: Bottom line from the academic and regulatory record: once a small-cap pump is visible to a retail trader (social spike, pre-market gap, top-mover list, halt), the expected return of going long is negative on every horizon measured. Robinhood herding events (top 0.5% daily holder increase; +14% event-day return, +11% of it at the open) are followed by about -5% over the next month (-9% for extreme events; -3%/-6% over 5 days), and a sell-after-herding strategy was right 63% of the time (Barber, Huang, Odean, Schwarz). Social-media message-volume spikes on OTC names earn +6.9% on the event day (after +4.1% the day before) and then -3.1% over the next 5 days, -5.3% when known promoters drive the spike (Renault 2017). Buyers on the heaviest stock-spam day lose 5.25% in two days while the spammer who bought the day before makes 4.9% (Frieder & Zittrain). Pump-and-dump participants at a German bank lost 28-30% on average per scheme (buy-and-hold from first tout: -53% mean, -70% median), with ~6-8% of active investors participating and 11% repeating (Leuz et al.). Crypto analogues compress the same curve into seconds: +25% and 148x volume in the first 70 seconds, insiders +18%, anyone entering more than a minute late loses (Li, Shin, Wang); 355 Binance/Yobit pumps averaged +65% within minutes and were a negative-sum game for everyone but organizers (Dhawan & Putnins). Short-squeeze candidates are a negative-EV long as a class: high-fee/high-utilization stocks earn -2.67%/month abnormal returns even though utilization >=90% makes a squeeze ~every 11 days vs once per 40 years at 25% (Schultz, JFQA 2024); the vendor models (IHS Markit) only show +7 bps open-to-close and +44-103 bps/month inside an already-shorted universe, and Ortex/S3 publish no verifiable squeeze win rates. Buying the first gap is worse than buying later: high-retail-attention stocks open high and fade intraday, with an implicit cost that often exceeds the half-spread (Berkman et al.), and high-MAX (lottery-return) stocks underperform by >1%/month (Bali et al.). The only documented positive-EV positions are (a) being the promoter/insider, (b) the first ~20 seconds of a crypto pump, (c) fading the move after a herding/social spike, (d) predicting the target before the pump (crypto only, 60% over 2.5 months in Xu & Livshits, unproven in equities), and (e) the small, slow +10 bps/week edge of aggregate retail order imbalance in small stocks absent attention spikes (Boehmer et al.). Day-trading base rates are brutal: 97% of persistent Brazilian day traders lost money and 97% of Taiwanese day traders are predicted to lose. Regulators now describe the 2024-2026 variant precisely: WhatsApp/Telegram 'investment clubs' ramp a $4-6 foreign-issuer Nasdaq Capital Market IPO over weeks or months then dump; FBI complaints up >=300% in 2025; SEC suspended 14 such issuers between Sept 2025 and Feb 2026 (QMMM +~1000% in <3 weeks, TCGL $8 to $300+ in two days), roughly a quarter of 250+ Nasdaq Capital Market IPOs since 2023 followed the promote-then-crash/suspend pattern, and Nasdaq's 2025-2026 rules ($15M float from IPO proceeds, $25M for China-based, discretion to deny listings, delisting after SEC suspension, $5M MVLS floor with no cure period) have cut small-cap IPOs from 23 in Q4 2025 to 5 in Q1 2026. For detection, the strongest published signals are promoter/bot provenance of the mentions (71% of suspicious financial tweets were bots; inorganic-campaign classifiers reach F1 0.97), structural issuer risk (FINRA 22-25 profile: <20M shares, <$25M raised, <$100M valuation, foreign issuer, nominee accounts), and microstructure 'rush order' bursts (crypto detectors hit precision 93-98% within 5-25 seconds). No regulatory or academic source quantifies how often LULD-halted runners close below the open; that number must come from your own backtest.

signals.name: Social message-volume spike (Renault event definition)
signals.definition: Daily message count for a cashtag > trailing-year mean + 2 standard deviations, with at least 20 messages that day and market cap >= $1M; minimum 20-day gap between events on the same ticker. Associated returns: +4.10% abnormal the day before, +6.88% on the event day, -3.11% cumulative over days +1 to +5 (-5.34% when promoter accounts drive the spike).
signals.data_needed: Per-ticker daily (ideally hourly) counts from StockTwits/X/Reddit; trailing-365-day mean and SD per ticker; market cap.
signals.timing: During (fires on the event day; the day-before run-up of +4.1% means the first leg is often already gone).
signals.source: Renault (2017), 'Market manipulation and suspicious stock recommendations on social media', EFMA WP / J. Banking & Finance; 7.2M tweets, 5,087 OTC firms, 635 events.

signals.name: Promoter / pump-tracker provenance of mentions
signals.definition: Share of event-day messages authored by accounts whose profile or history contains promotional markers ('promote', 'tout', 'compensation', newsletter/promo-site links) or by accounts dedicated to tracking pumps (e.g., @ThePumpTracker, @PUMPSandDUMPS). Renault manually classified 156 promoter accounts; promoter-driven events reversed -5.34% over 5 days vs -3.11% for all events.
signals.data_needed: Author metadata (bio text, links, account age), a maintained promoter list, mention-level author IDs.
signals.timing: During (same day as the spike), can be pre-market when promo posts precede the open.
signals.source: Renault (2017); SEC 2017 enforcement sweep on undisclosed paid articles (Lit. Rel. 23802) for the keyword list.

signals.name: Inorganic / bot share of mentions and cashtag piggybacking
signals.definition: Fraction of authors flagged as bots by a spambot classifier; in the Cresci et al. sample 71% of authors of suspicious financial tweets were bots and 37% were later suspended. Piggybacking pattern: a low-cap cashtag co-posted with 3+ mega-cap cashtags in the same message. Tardelli et al. report F1 = 0.97 for detecting inorganic financial campaigns and R2 = 0.81 (MAE 4.9 pp) for estimating the bot share of a viral discussion; the more viral a stock, the larger the artificial share.
signals.data_needed: Author-level features (account age, posting cadence, follower ratios, repeated text), co-mention graph of cashtags, optional bot classifier.
signals.timing: Pre-market to during (campaigns typically start before price moves).
signals.source: Cresci, Lillo, Regoli, Tardelli, Tesconi (2019) ACM TWEB 'Cashtag piggybacking'; Tardelli, Tesconi, Cresci (2022) 'Detecting inorganic financial campaigns on Twitter'.

signals.name: Retail herding / top-mover attention event
signals.definition: Barber et al. definition: stock is in the top 0.5% of daily percentage increase in Robinhood holders (4,884 events, ~9/day) or 'extreme' = +1,000 holders and +50% vs prior day (900 events). Event-day abnormal return +14% (+42% extreme), mean opening return +11%; next-month abnormal return about -5% (-9%); 5-day -3% (-6%). Sell-after-event/rebuy-5-days-later BHAR +3.5% (+6.4%), positive 63% of the time. Effect concentrated in market caps < $1B. Practical proxy today: top-0.5% daily retail order imbalance (sub-penny BJZZ method) or membership on top-gainers lists.
signals.data_needed: Retail order imbalance from TAQ sub-penny prints (BJZZ), or holder-count data; daily top-mover lists; market cap.
signals.timing: During (event day); reversal plays out over 5-20 trading days.
signals.source: Barber, Huang, Odean, Schwarz (2022) 'Attention-Induced Trading and Returns: Evidence from Robinhood Users', Review of Finance; Boehmer, Jones, Zhang, Zhang (2021) JF for the imbalance proxy.

signals.name: Attention-driven opening gap (overnight-return reversal)
signals.definition: Large positive overnight (close-to-open) return in a stock with high prior-day retail attention (abnormal volume, extreme return, news). Berkman et al.: positive overnight returns reversed intraday because the open prints high relative to intraday prices; concentrated in retail-attention, hard-to-value, costly-to-arbitrage stocks; the implicit cost of buying at the open frequently exceeds the effective half-spread. Aboody et al.: high-overnight-return stocks underperform over longer horizons.
signals.data_needed: Prior close, pre-market/open price, prior-day volume and return, news flag.
signals.timing: Pre-market / first 5 minutes.
signals.source: Berkman, Koch, Tuttle, Zhang (2012) JFQA 'Paying Attention: Overnight Returns and the Hidden Cost of Buying at the Open'; Aboody, Even-Tov, Lehavy, Trueman (2018) JFQA.

signals.name: MAX / lottery-return flag
signals.definition: Stock's maximum single-day return over the prior month is in the top decile of the cross-section. High-MAX decile underperforms low-MAX decile by more than 1% per month, raw and risk-adjusted (reported ~ -1.03% raw, -1.18% alpha in the original paper).
signals.data_needed: Daily returns for the universe; monthly decile ranks.
signals.timing: Late (monthly cross-sectional; useful as a bag-holder warning on any recent runner).
signals.source: Bali, Cakici, Whitelaw (2011) JFE 'Maxing Out'.

signals.name: Short-squeeze candidate (academic/vendor definitions)
signals.definition: Schultz: squeeze = shares available to lend fall below shares on loan (all-lender) or both decline equally on the same day via recalls (current-lender); occurs on 0.183% / 0.469% of stock-days; utilization is the single best predictor (utilization >=90% implies a squeeze about every 11 days vs once per 40 years at 25%). IHS Markit model: 3-SD price move vs prior 60 days over 1-3 days followed by a 5-consecutive-day decline in shares on loan; top-decile candidates had a 78% higher squeeze probability vs a 0.94% base rate, +7 bps open-to-close, +44/+103 bps 1-month vs universe/bottom decile. S3 Partners Squeeze Score: >70 'trouble', >=90 'significantly higher risk', 100 max. Ortex: three signal types from SI, utilization, cost-to-borrow, price and their rates of change (thresholds not published).
signals.data_needed: Daily securities-lending data (utilization, shares on loan, lendable supply, fee) from Ortex/S3/IHS (paid); FINRA bi-monthly short interest is too lagged.
signals.timing: During (the price spike is part of the definition, so identification is after the first move); utilization/fee give a pre-market structural score.
signals.source: Schultz (2024) JFQA 'Short Squeezes and Their Consequences'; IHS Markit 'US Short Squeeze Model' (May 2015); Allen, Haas, Pirovano, Tengulov (SFI 23-63): ~25% of unique stocks have a squeeze in a given year; S3/Ortex public pages.

signals.name: Ramp-and-dump IPO structural profile (FINRA 22-25 / Nasdaq IM-5101-3)
signals.definition: Exchange-listed issuer with: IPO of fewer than 20M shares, less than $25M raised, valuation under $100M, $4-$6 offer price; Cayman/BVI shell with operations in China, Hong Kong, Singapore or SE Asia; microcap underwriter with prior volatile deals; concentrated/nominee holders; listed within the last ~12 months (FINRA 2025: the spike moved from IPO day in 2022-23 to 'weeks or months after' in 2024). Observed outcomes: ~1 in 4 of 250+ Nasdaq Capital Market IPOs since 2023 were WhatsApp-promoted then crashed or were SEC-suspended; one underwriter's 11 deals: 10 surged (one $4 to $100+ in a month), 9 now 54-98% below IPO price, >$2B lost from peaks.
signals.data_needed: EDGAR F-1/S-1 and 424B (shares, proceeds, underwriter, jurisdiction), float and insider ownership, listing date, OTC/Nasdaq tier.
signals.timing: Pre-market (static risk score computed nightly).
signals.source: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25 (Nov 2022); FINRA 2025 and 2026 Annual Regulatory Oversight Reports; Nasdaq IM-5101-3 (SEC-approved Dec 19, 2025); Bloomberg graphics (2026) and Philadelphia Inquirer (May 12, 2026) on Bancroft Capital IPOs.

signals.name: Group-chat ramp signature (FINRA/FBI mechanics)
signals.definition: Multi-week or multi-month steady rise on rising volume in a low-priced, low-volume listed stock with no filings/news, accompanied by clustered retail buying at specific times/prices (victims are told which broker, what to buy, when and at what price). FBI PSA I-070325-PSA: >=300% increase in ramp-and-dump complaints in 2025 vs 2024. Collapse signature: 70-93% single-session drops (TEN: $100+ to ~$31 next day; OST: $9.40 to $0.55 intraday, -93%; QMMM +~1000% in <3 weeks then 10-day SEC suspension).
signals.data_needed: Daily OHLCV, news/8-K feed, retail imbalance by time-of-day, issuer domicile.
signals.timing: During (ramp phase lasts weeks, so it is detectable before the dump, but direction of the next day is not).
signals.source: FINRA Investor Insight 'Investment Group Imposter Scams' (Dec 9, 2025); FBI IC3 PSA (Jul 3, 2025); CSA Investor Alert (Apr 16, 2026); SEC trading suspensions Sept 2025-Feb 2026 (securitieslawyer101 summary); investinglive OST postmortem (Aug 2025, trade press).

signals.name: Filer / capital-structure red flags
signals.definition: Any of: Form 15 deregistration or delinquent 10-K/20-F; registered direct offering or ATM priced far below market (OST: $5M RDO at $0.55 vs pumped price, 90%+ discount); multiple reverse splits; large warrant overhang; going-concern language; Nasdaq deficiency notices; recent increase in authorized shares. SEC DERA (White 2016): promoted OTC stocks and lower-disclosure tiers have the worst investor outcomes; OTC average/median annual returns about -27%/-37% (Eraker & Ready).
signals.data_needed: EDGAR full-text and form-type feed (8-K, 424B, S-3, Form 15), Nasdaq notices.
signals.timing: Pre-market (nightly batch).
signals.source: SEC DERA, White (Dec 16, 2016) 'Outcomes of Investing in OTC Stocks'; investinglive OST postmortem; Massoud, Ullah, Scholnick (2016) J. Fin. Stability on secret promotion coinciding with insider selling.

signals.name: Rush-order / aggressive-buy burst (crypto real-time detectors)
signals.definition: Within 25-second chunks over a 7-hour window: count and standard deviation of 'rush orders' (market buys filled immediately), trade count, volume and price change vs rolling baseline; random forest on these features detected Binance pumps with precision 93.1%, recall 91.4%, F1 92.0% (104 events) within 5 seconds, and later precision 98.2%, recall 91.2%, F1 94.5% at 25-second latency (~900 events). Pump magnitude for reference: +25% and 148x volume in first 70 s; 83.5% of targets traded under $1M/day.
signals.data_needed: Tick-level trades with aggressor side (from TAQ trade conditions or a consolidated feed), 1-25 second bars; equity transfer untested.
signals.timing: First seconds to first 5 minutes.
signals.source: La Morgia, Mei, Sassi, Stefa (2020) ICCCN 'Pump and Dumps in the Bitcoin Era'; La Morgia et al. (2021/2023) 'The Doge of Wall Street'; Li, Shin, Wang (JFQA) for magnitudes.

signals.name: Price/volume anomaly thresholds (Kamps & Kleinberg)
signals.definition: Over a 12-24 hour estimation window: volume increase threshold between 25% and 400% (configurable), price increase threshold 3-10%, and dump detection when price falls below rolling average plus 1 SD; pumps shortened to seconds-minutes to peak.
signals.data_needed: Minute OHLCV, rolling mean/SD per ticker.
signals.timing: During.
signals.source: Kamps & Kleinberg (2018) Crime Science 'To the moon: defining and detecting cryptocurrency pump-and-dumps'.

signals.name: Forum-language pump classifier (penny-stock subreddits)
signals.definition: Posts on r/pennystocks and r/RobinHoodPennyStocks matched to a price/volume profile with a flat 5-day baseline followed by a spike; dumps typically within four days of the post. Best text model: accuracy 85%, F1 62% (posts+comments) to 67% (posts only).
signals.data_needed: Reddit posts/comments with timestamps, ticker extraction, daily OHLCV for a 9-day window.
signals.timing: During (post day), gives roughly a 1-4 day window before the dump.
signals.source: Nam & Skillicorn (2023) arXiv 2301.11403 'Detecting Pump&Dump Stock Market Manipulation from Online Forums'.

signals.name: Finfluencer skill tier of the source
signals.definition: On StockTwits, 28% of finfluencers are skilled, 16% unskilled, 56% 'anti-skilled' (negative abnormal returns); anti-skilled accounts have more followers and ride return/sentiment momentum. WSB due-diligence posts predicted returns pre-GameStop (+1.1% 2-day, +2% 1-month, ~+5% 1-quarter) but have had no predictive power since Jan 2021.
signals.data_needed: Author-level historical calls and realized returns; post timestamps.
signals.timing: During (at post time).
signals.source: Kakhbod, Kazempour, Livdan, Schuerhoff (2025) 'Finfluencers' (AEA 2025); Bradley, Hanousek, Jame, Xiao (2024) 'Place Your Bets?' Review of Finance.

signals.name: Search-attention surge
signals.definition: Abnormal increase in Google Search Volume Index for the ticker predicts higher prices over the next 2 weeks and reversal within the year (Russell 3000, 2004-2008).
signals.data_needed: Google Trends weekly SVI per ticker.
signals.timing: Late (weekly data).
signals.source: Da, Engelberg, Gao (2011) JF 'In Search of Attention'.

signals.name: LULD halt and resumption
signals.definition: Tier 2 stocks above $3 trade inside +/-10% bands (doubled to 20% in the first and last minutes of the day); $0.75-$3 bands are +/-20%; 5-minute pause when a limit state persists 15 seconds. SEC DERA: after a trading pause, prices typically revert to within the prior bands, i.e., many pauses are liquidity gaps rather than fundamental moves. Hautsch & Horvath: pauses improve price discovery during the break but raise post-pause volatility and worsen liquidity. No published statistic on the share of halted small-cap runners closing below the open (unverified).
signals.data_needed: SIP halt/resume messages with reason codes, LULD band data, intraday prices.
signals.timing: During (resumption).
signals.source: SEC DERA, Moise & Flaherty (Mar 2017) 'Limit Up-Limit Down Pilot Plan and Associated Events'; Hautsch & Horvath (2019) JFE 'How effective are trading pauses?'; LULD Plan parameters.

facts.claim: In a sample of 110,000+ German retail investors and 421-470 pump-and-dump touts (2006-2014), about 6% (NBER version) to 8% (published Management Science version) of active investors bought into at least one scheme; the average return per tout investment was -28% to -30%, the average investment was EUR 6,972 (11.4% of portfolio), buy-and-hold 120-day returns from the first tout date averaged -53% (median -70%), 11% of participants repeated and still lost 24% on average, and >35% of participants were penny-stock day traders or similar active speculators.
facts.source: Leuz, Meyer, Muhn, Soltes, Hackethal, NBER WP 24083 (full text extracted) and Management Science abstract

facts.claim: On OTC names, a Twitter message-volume spike (mean + 2 SD, >=20 tweets) coincides with +6.88% abnormal return on the event day after +4.10% the prior day, followed by -3.11% over days +1 to +5; events driven by 156 identified promoter accounts reverse -5.34% in 5 days. Sample: 7.2M tweets, 248,748 users, 5,087 OTC firms, 635 events.
facts.source: Renault (2017) EFMA working paper / readkong copy

facts.claim: Stock spam: 75,000+ touts (2004-2005). Buying the day before heavy touting and selling the next morning returned +4.9% (about +6% for the heaviest touts); buying on the heaviest-tout day and holding two days returned -5.25% (-7% for the most heavily touted).
facts.source: Frieder & Zittrain (2007) 'Spam Works', Berkman Klein Center / Hastings Comm & Ent LJ

facts.claim: Stock spam e-mails move returns, intraday volatility and volume with no lasting price effect; liquidity determines success and spamming on successive days extends the window in which spammers can liquidate.
facts.source: Hanke & Hauser (2008) Journal of Financial Markets, as summarized in Siering (2021) and search results

facts.claim: SEC DERA analysis of 1.8M OTC trades by 200,000+ individuals: the typical OTC investment return is severely negative and worse for stocks that experience a promotional campaign or sit in lower-disclosure tiers; cited literature puts average/median annual OTC returns at -27%/-37% (2001-2010).
facts.source: White, J.T. (Dec 16, 2016) 'Outcomes of Investing in OTC Stocks', SEC DERA white paper (full text extracted)

facts.claim: Secretly paid stock promotion raises price and volume at promotion start, coincides with insider selling, and reverses when regulators act; a secondary source attributes +11.94% 5-day CAR during promotion and -32.94% over five days upon disclosure to this paper (numbers not verified against the original).
facts.source: Massoud, Ullah, Scholnick (2016) Journal of Financial Stability 26:45-61; stockwirex.com summary for the percentages

facts.claim: YouTube-promoted stocks reportedly return ~+7.9% on release day and ~+11.8% over five days, fully reverting by day 30 (figures only available via a secondary trade source; original not retrieved).
facts.source: Leite et al. (2025) 'Pay to Pump', Applied Economics Letters, via stockwirex.com

facts.claim: SEC-prosecuted manipulation cases show prices rising through the manipulation period and falling afterward; manipulators are typically informed parties; prices and liquidity are higher when manipulators sell than when they buy.
facts.source: Aggarwal & Wu (2006) Journal of Business 79(4)

facts.claim: On StockTwits, 28% of finfluencers are skilled, 16% unskilled and 56% anti-skilled; anti-skilled finfluencers have more followers and ride return and sentiment momentum.
facts.source: Kakhbod, Kazempour, Livdan, Schuerhoff, 'Finfluencers', AEA 2025 program

facts.claim: WallStreetBets due-diligence 'buy' posts earned +1.1% over two days, +2% over a month and ~5% over a quarter with no reversal before the January 2021 GameStop episode; afterward their predictive power vanished as posts shifted to price-pressure and attention-grabbing stocks.
facts.source: Bradley, Hanousek, Jame, Xiao, 'Place Your Bets? The Value of Investment Research on Reddit's Wallstreetbets', Review of Finance

facts.claim: Crypto pumps (about 500 hand-collected Telegram events): price +25%, volume 148x and 10-second absolute returns of 15% in the first 70 seconds; a ~5% run-up begins five minutes before the announcement; insiders earn ~18%; outsiders entering more than a minute after the start lose >1% on average (about 2% when trading against insiders); most effects disappear within an hour.
facts.source: Li, Shin, Wang, 'Cryptocurrency Pump-and-Dump Schemes', JFQA; CLS Blue Sky summary

facts.claim: 355 announced pumps on Binance and Yobit over seven months produced average price distortions of 65% within minutes that reverted shortly after; the schemes are a negative-sum game for everyone except the organizers, and participation is explained by overconfidence and gambling preferences.
facts.source: Dhawan & Putnins (2023) 'A New Wolf in Town?', Review of Finance 27(3)

facts.claim: Nearly 5,000 crypto pumps on Discord/Telegram: the coin's obscurity (low rank/volume) is the most important determinant of pump profitability.
facts.source: Hamrick, Rouhi, Mukherjee, Feder, Gandal, Moore, Vasek, CEPR DP13404 / Information Processing & Management (2021)

facts.claim: A model predicting which coin will be pumped before 412 Telegram pumps (2018-2019) reportedly yielded up to 60% return on small retail positions over 2.5 months; this is crypto-specific and the equity analogue is unproven.
facts.source: Xu & Livshits (2019) USENIX Security, arXiv 1811.10109

facts.claim: Real-time crypto pump detectors using 25-second chunks and 'rush order' features reach precision 93.1%/recall 91.4% (104 Binance events, detection within 5 s) and later precision 98.2%/recall 91.2%/F1 94.5% at 25-second latency (~900 events); 83.5% of targets traded under $1M/day and VIP members received signals 0.5-10 s earlier than others.
facts.source: La Morgia et al. (2020) ICCCN arXiv 2005.06610; La Morgia et al. (2021/2023) arXiv 2105.00733

facts.claim: Kamps & Kleinberg's anomaly criteria: 12-24 hour estimation window, volume-increase thresholds of 25%-400%, price-increase thresholds of 3-10%, dump flagged when price falls below rolling average + 1 SD; pumps now peak within seconds to minutes.
facts.source: Kamps & Kleinberg (2018) Crime Science 7:18, via search summary (article page blocked)

facts.claim: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25 (Nov 17, 2022) flagged 'ramp and dump' in small-cap IPOs, mostly China/HK-linked, with risk factors: fewer than 20M shares issued, less than $25M raised, valuation under $100M, foreign issuers/broker-dealers, concentrated holdings, nominee and omnibus accounts at U.S. firms.
facts.source: FINRA Regulatory Notice 22-25; Olshan summary

facts.claim: FINRA's 2025 oversight report says that by 2024 the unusual price increases shifted from IPO day to weeks or months after IPO, with nominee accounts accumulating then liquidating into retail buying generated by social-media 'investment club' grooming scams; the 2026 report (Dec 9, 2025) again lists manipulative trading in small-cap exchange-listed equities as a priority.
facts.source: FINRA 2025 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report (Manipulative Trading section); FINRA 2026 report press release

facts.claim: FINRA Investor Insight (Dec 9, 2025): scammers first recommend a well-known stock, then move victims into a low-priced low-volume listed stock, tell them which broker-dealer to use and what, when and at what price to buy, until victims cannot sell and the price crashes; the FBI's July 3, 2025 PSA reported at least a 300% increase in ramp-and-dump complaints in 2025 vs 2024.
facts.source: finra.org/investors/insights/investment-group-imposter-scams; FBI IC3 PSA I-070325-PSA

facts.claim: Canadian regulators issued a ramp-and-dump investor alert on April 16, 2026 describing the same WhatsApp/Discord/Telegram investment-group pattern.
facts.source: CSA Investor Alert (NSSC PDF dated 2026-04-16); investright.org

facts.claim: The SEC formed a Cross-Border Task Force on Sept 5, 2025 targeting pump-and-dump schemes in foreign-based issuers and the gatekeepers (auditors, underwriters) that bring them to U.S. markets.
facts.source: Mayer Brown and Akin Gump client alerts, Sept 2025

facts.claim: Between late Sept 2025 and early Feb 2026 the SEC issued 14 ten-day trading suspensions, all foreign issuers on Nasdaq/NYSE, citing potential social-media manipulation by unknown persons; examples: QMMM ($4 IPO, +~1000% in under three weeks to $300+ intraday), TCGL ($8 to $300+ in two days), MCTA ($4 to $29), SDM (collapsed 86-88%); most remained halted or moved to OTC afterward.
facts.source: securitieslawyer101.com (Feb 3, 2026); Bloomberg Law; mdf-law.com on MCTA

facts.claim: Nasdaq listing-rule timeline: Apr 11, 2025 effective - MVUPHS must come solely from IPO proceeds ($5M under net-income standard, $15M otherwise); Dec 18, 2025 approved / Jan 17, 2026 effective - $15M minimum public float under the net-income standard; Dec 19, 2025 - IM-5101-3 discretion to deny listings based on manipulation-susceptibility factors (jurisdiction, advisor/underwriter history of volatile deals, float/allocation, management familiarity); May 14, 2026 - $25M minimum IPO proceeds for China/HK/Macau-based companies; Jun 3, 2026 - IM-5101-4 authority to delist after an SEC trading suspension; Jul 22, 2026 - $5M MVLS continued-listing floor with immediate suspension after 30 consecutive business days and no cure period.
facts.source: K&L Gates, Greenberg Traurig, Dechert, Morgan Lewis, Duane Morris, Dorsey client alerts; securities-law-blog.com; Nasdaq press release Sept 3, 2025

facts.claim: Small-cap IPO counts fell from 23 in Q4 2025 to 5 in Q1 2026 after IM-5101-3; foreign microcap IPOs 'dried up' by mid-2026.
facts.source: securities-law-blog.com (Dec 23, 2025 and Q2 2026 wrap); The Star / Bloomberg (Jul 25, 2026)

facts.claim: Bloomberg's 2026 analysis found that about a quarter of the 250+ companies that listed on Nasdaq's smallest tier since 2023 were promoted in WhatsApp group chats and then crashed or were SEC-suspended; almost 100 Asia-based microcaps debuted on U.S. exchanges in 2025.
facts.source: Bloomberg graphics '2026 Wall Street apparent pump-and-dump investor scam' (via search summary; article paywalled)

facts.claim: One microcap underwriter's 11 completed IPOs ($4-$6 offer prices, ~$100M raised, 10 based in Singapore/Hong Kong): 10 surged (one from $4 to $100+ within a month), 9 traded 54-98% below IPO price as of May 1, 2026, with more than $2B of peak market value erased; TEN Holdings went from a $6 IPO to $100+ on Feb 13, 2025, ~$31 the next day, $18 four days later and under $1.50 later.
facts.source: Philadelphia Inquirer (May 12, 2026)

facts.claim: Ostin Technology (OST): promoted via WhatsApp/Telegram by impersonated U.S. advisers with AI-generated celebrity videos and a fake OLED-acquisition rumor; the company had deregistered from SEC reporting and announced a $5M direct offering at $0.55 on Apr 15, 2025; on Jun 26, 2025 it fell ~93% intraday from a $9.40 peak to close at $0.55 and reached ~$0.08 by early July; the FBI issued a bulletin on Jul 17, 2025.
facts.source: investinglive.com postmortem (Aug 6, 2025) - trade press, partially unverified

facts.claim: Robinhood herding events (top 0.5% daily holder increase; 4,884 events; extreme = +1,000 users and +50%; 900 events): event-day abnormal return +14% (+42%) with mean opening return +11%; subsequent month about -5% (-9%); 5-day -3% (-6%); selling after the event and rebuying five days later produced BHAR +3.5% (+6.4%) and was positive 63% of the time; negative post-event returns concentrated in stocks under $1B market cap; about one-third of herding events were large losers because the Top Movers list ranks by absolute return.
facts.source: Barber, Huang, Odean, Schwarz, 'Attention-Induced Trading and Returns: Evidence from Robinhood Users' (SSRN 3715077 full text extracted; Review of Finance 2022)

facts.claim: Individual investors are net buyers of attention-grabbing stocks (news, abnormal volume, extreme one-day returns, both positive and negative); attention-driven buying does not generate superior returns and the stocks individuals buy subsequently underperform the ones they sell.
facts.source: Barber & Odean (2008) 'All That Glitters', Review of Financial Studies 21(2) (full text extracted; magnitude tables not quoted)

facts.claim: Positive overnight returns are reversed intraday because the open is high relative to intraday prices; the pattern is concentrated in stocks with recent retail attention, hard-to-value and costly-to-arbitrage stocks, and high-sentiment periods; the implicit cost of buying high-attention stocks at the open frequently exceeds the effective half-spread.
facts.source: Berkman, Koch, Tuttle, Zhang (2012) JFQA 47(4):715-741

facts.claim: Stocks with high overnight returns underperform over longer horizons (sentiment proxy); momentum and reversal strategy profits accrue overnight, with individuals favoring overnight trading and institutions intraday.
facts.source: Aboody, Even-Tov, Lehavy, Trueman (2018) JFQA; Lou, Polk, Skouras (2019) JFE

facts.claim: An increase in Google search volume for a ticker predicts higher prices over the next two weeks and an eventual reversal within the year (Russell 3000, 2004-2008).
facts.source: Da, Engelberg, Gao (2011) Journal of Finance

facts.claim: The highest-MAX decile (largest single-day return in the prior month) underperforms the lowest by more than 1% per month, raw and risk-adjusted.
facts.source: Bali, Cakici, Whitelaw (2011) JFE 'Maxing Out'

facts.claim: Marketable retail order imbalance (sub-penny method) predicts about +10 bps over the following week (~5% annualized), stronger in small, low-priced stocks and persisting up to 12 weeks; this is the opposite sign to the attention-herding result, which is specific to extreme concentrated buying episodes.
facts.source: Boehmer, Jones, Zhang, Zhang (2021) Journal of Finance 'Tracking Retail Investor Activity'

facts.claim: Day trading base rates: of Brazilians who began day trading equity futures in 2013-2015 and persisted more than 300 days, 97% lost money, 1.1% earned more than minimum wage and 0.5% more than a bank teller's starting salary, with no evidence of learning; in Taiwan (1992-2006) about 97% of day traders are predicted to lose going forward, 74% of day-trading volume comes from traders with a history of losses, and more than 75% quit within two years.
facts.source: Chague, De-Losso, Giovannetti (2020) 'Day Trading for a Living?'; Barber, Lee, Liu, Odean 'Learning Fast or Slow' (RAPS 2020) and 'The Cross-Section of Speculator Skill' (2014)

facts.claim: Short squeezes (IHS Markit 2006-2019): all-lender squeezes occur on 0.183% of stock-days and current-lender squeezes on 0.469%; utilization is the single best predictor (>=90% utilization implies a squeeze about every 11 days vs once per 40 years at 25%); high-fee/high-utilization stocks earn abnormal returns of -2.67% per month versus +0.56% for low-fee/low-utilization stocks, so buying squeeze candidates is unprofitable on average.
facts.source: Schultz (2024) JFQA 'Short Squeezes and Their Consequences', via Evidence Investor summary

facts.claim: About 25% of unique U.S. and EU stocks experience a short squeeze in a given year; events are rare and short-lived with a recent U.S. uptick; EU short-position disclosure rules did not increase squeeze frequency.
facts.source: Allen, Haas, Pirovano, Tengulov, SFI Research Paper 23-63 / Harvard Law corpgov summary

facts.claim: A long-low-fee/short-high-fee decile portfolio earns 1.45%/month gross (1.55% four-factor alpha; 0.92% net of borrow cost); anomalies essentially do not exist among the 80% of stocks with the lowest fees; short-side anomaly returns are concentrated in 'special' hard-to-borrow stocks with the lowest lendable supply.
facts.source: Drechsler & Drechsler (2014) NBER WP 20282; Beneish, Lee, Nichols (2015) 'In Short Supply'

facts.claim: IHS Markit's US Short Squeeze Model defines a squeeze as a 3-SD price move vs the prior 60 days over 1-3 days followed by a 5-consecutive-day decline in shares on loan; top-decile candidates had a 78% higher squeeze likelihood than the 0.94% base rate and earned +7 bps open-to-close (+12 bps vs bottom decile), +19/+30 bps over two weeks and +44/+103 bps over one month.
facts.source: IHS Markit Research Signals, 'US Short Squeeze Model' (May 2015, full text extracted)

facts.claim: Ortex's short-squeeze signals combine short interest, utilization, cost-to-borrow, price and their rates of change in three signal types; the public performance page gives aggregate signal returns (e.g., EPS signals) but no squeeze-specific win rate, and warns any signal can trigger for the wrong reasons. S3 Partners' Squeeze Score flags >70 as trouble and >=90 as significantly higher risk while stating a high score does not guarantee a squeeze.
facts.source: public.ortex.com/trading-signals; BNN Bloomberg / Benzinga coverage of S3 Squeeze Score

facts.claim: SEC DERA's LULD study (2013-2015 data) finds that after a trading pause prices revert to within the price bands in effect before the pause, indicating many pauses are liquidity gaps rather than fundamental moves; Tier 2 stocks above $3 have +/-10% bands (doubled at open/close), and Tier 2 generated over two million straddle states in under four months.
facts.source: Moise & Flaherty (Mar 2017), SEC DERA white paper (full text extracted)

facts.claim: Single-stock trading pauses improve price discovery during the break but have adverse effects on price stability and liquidity afterward; they do not cool markets but cause extra volatility.
facts.source: Hautsch & Horvath (2019) JFE 'How effective are trading pauses?' (abstract)

facts.claim: No academic, SEC, FINRA or exchange source was found that reports the fraction of LULD-halted small-cap runners that close below the open or below the halt price; trader-blog statements ('plenty continue, plenty reverse violently') are unquantified. This item is unverifiable from public sources.
facts.source: Searches of sec.gov DERA, Nasdaq 'All about LULDs', tapeboard.com halt logs, trade-ideas.com

facts.claim: Reddit penny-stock pump detection: posts matched to a flat 5-day price/volume baseline followed by a spike; dumps typically occur within four days; best text classifier reaches 85% accuracy and 62-67% F1.
facts.source: Nam & Skillicorn (2023) arXiv 2301.11403 (full text extracted)

facts.claim: On Twitter, 71% of authors of suspicious financial tweets were classified as bots and 37% were later suspended; bots promote low-value stocks by piggybacking on high-value cashtags; detectors of inorganic financial campaigns achieve F1 = 0.97, and the more viral a stock the larger its bot-driven share.
facts.source: Cresci, Lillo, Regoli, Tardelli, Tesconi (2019) ACM TWEB; Tardelli, Tesconi, Cresci (2022)

facts.claim: Historical SEC trading suspensions are associated with substantial, largely permanent devaluation and prolonged negative abnormal returns after resumption, with only a small second-day rebound.
facts.source: Ferris, Kumar, Wolfe (1992) Financial Review; Howe & Schlarbaum (1986) JFQA; Kabir (1994)

facts.claim: A FINRA Foundation survey (Apr 2026) reportedly found 61% of investors aged 18-34 have made an investment decision based on a social-media personality's recommendation (26% overall, ~6% for 55+).
facts.source: stockwirex.com citing FINRA Foundation (not verified against the FINRA release)

recommendations: Set the detector's default posture to 'warn/fade', not 'buy': every measured post-signal long horizon is negative (5-day -3% to -6% and 1-month -5% to -9% after retail herding; -3.1% to -5.3% over 5 days after social spikes; -5.25% over 2 days for tout-day buyers; -28% per pump for participants; -2.67%/month for squeeze candidates; >1%/month for high-MAX names). Treat any alert as a bag-holder warning first and a long candidate only if it passes an explicit early-phase gate.

Define the early-phase gate numerically and time-box it: the equity analogue of the crypto window (profits only in the first ~20 s, losses after 60 s) is the first few minutes after a fresh social/volume anomaly with no prior-day run-up (Renault's +4.1% day-before means most alerts are already late). Require: no prior-day run-up above ~5%, mention volume just crossed mean + 2 SD, promoter/bot share below a threshold you calibrate (start at 30%), and exit by a hard time stop (minutes to one session). Never hold overnight into the attention open: the open is where high-attention stocks print their highs (mean opening return +11% in herding events, then fade).

Do not buy the first gap. Berkman et al. show buying attention stocks at the open costs more than the half-spread and the overnight gain reverses intraday; if a long is taken at all, wait for the intraday reversal to exhaust (the 'dip') rather than the open, and only in names that are not on the ramp-and-dump structural list.

Run a nightly structural risk score and use it to gate real-time alerts: foreign (Cayman/BVI/China/HK/Singapore) issuer, Nasdaq Capital Market or NYSE American, IPO within 12-18 months at $4-$6 with <20M shares / <$25M raised / <$100M valuation, microcap underwriter with prior volatile deals, deregistered/delinquent filer, recent reverse splits or discounted direct offerings, tiny float with concentrated holders. Any real-time spike in a name scoring high here should emit a 'likely ramp-and-dump' phone alert that explicitly says do not buy; a quarter of Nasdaq Capital Market IPOs since 2023 ended in a crash or SEC suspension.

Make source provenance a first-class feature in the rules pass and the Claude pass: fraction of mentions from known promoter accounts (Renault's 'promote/tout/compensation/newsletter' profile keywords), bot-likeness (account age, cadence, cashtag piggybacking with mega-caps), WhatsApp/Telegram 'investment club' invitations, impersonated advisers or deepfake videos, acquisition rumors with no 8-K, and finfluencer track record (56% of StockTwits finfluencers are anti-skilled and have the most followers). Have Claude label each survivor as organic-news / paid-promotion / coordinated-ramp / unknown and route only organic-news to any long consideration.

Use published thresholds as starting rules, then calibrate on your own log: message volume > trailing-year mean + 2 SD with >=20 messages; minute-bar volume +25% to +400% over a 12-24h baseline with price +3-10%; top-0.5% daily retail order imbalance change; MAX-decile membership; utilization >=90% or fee spikes for squeeze risk; a 3-SD price move vs the prior 60 days. Expect high false-positive rates from the raw price/volume rules; the social-provenance and structural layers are what reduce them.

Treat short-squeeze screens as risk flags, not longs: utilization >=90% makes a squeeze likely (about one per 11 days) but the same stocks lose 2.67%/month on average and vendor squeeze models only show single-digit-bps intraday edges inside heavily shorted universes. If you keep a squeeze module, require paid daily lending data (utilization, shares on loan, fee) rather than FINRA bi-monthly short interest, and backtest Ortex/S3-style claims yourself because neither publishes a squeeze win rate.

Build the LULD statistic you could not find: log every Tier 2 halt (reason code, direction, price at halt, resume price, open, close, next-day close) for stocks under ~$20 and compute the share that close below the open and below the halt price, by number of halts that day. SEC DERA and Hautsch-Horvath imply resumptions revert toward prior bands and add volatility, so default to treating a second or third up-halt in a session as a sell/avoid signal until your own data says otherwise.

Instrument outcome tracking from day one: for every alert store entry time, signal type, structural score, and realized returns at +5 min, +30 min, close, +1 day, +5 days, +20 days. The literature's hit rates (63% for fading herding events, 0.9% base rate for squeezes, ~1-in-4 crash rate for recent microcap IPOs) give you priors to test against; publish your own precision/recall before trusting any long signal with real money.

Account for the 2026 regime shift when weighting data: Nasdaq's rules (float from IPO proceeds, $15M float, $25M for China-based issuers, discretion to deny listings, delisting after SEC suspension, $5M MVLS floor) have shrunk new small-cap IPOs from 23 to 5 per quarter, so FINRA already reports the ramp moving to names listed months earlier and the next migration is likely to older sub-$5M microcaps and OTC names. Keep the structural model keyed on issuer characteristics, not just listing age.

Keep the day-trading base rates in the UI: 97% of persistent day traders lose, and participants in pump schemes who sold early still averaged -28%. Size any early-phase long as a lottery ticket (small, capped daily count, hard stops) and never average down into a collapse; the dump leg has been 70-93% in a single session in 2025 cases.

Consider a reporting path rather than a trading path for clear coordinated-ramp detections (SEC TCR / FINRA), since trading along with a manipulation you have identified carries legal risk and, per the evidence, little expected profit for late entrants.
open_questions: What fraction of LULD-halted small-cap runners close below the open or below the first halt price? No academic, SEC, FINRA, Nasdaq or vendor source quantifies this; it has to come from your own tick data.

Do the crypto 'rush order' detectors (precision 93-98% within 5-25 seconds) transfer to U.S. equities, where announced pumps are rare, LULD bands interrupt the move, and aggressor-side flags must be inferred from trade conditions rather than exchange data?

Are the Massoud et al. (+11.94% / -32.94%) and Leite et al. 'Pay to Pump' (+7.9% / +11.8% / flat by day 30) figures accurate? Both were only available through a secondary trade source; originals were not retrieved.

Which investor types in Leuz et al. avoid losses? The paper says some types (penny-stock day traders who sell early) 'should not be viewed as falling prey', but the type-level return table was not extracted; the published Management Science version also reports 8% participation and 470 schemes vs 6% and 421 in the NBER draft.

What predicts squeezes in Allen, Haas, Pirovano, Tengulov (SFI 23-63) beyond the 25%-of-firms-per-year prevalence figure, and what are post-squeeze returns in their sample? Only the abstract was accessible.
What is the magnitude (not just sign) of the post-attention underperformance in Barber & Odean (2008)? The full text was extracted but the return tables were not quoted here.

How many SEC social-media-manipulation suspensions have occurred since February 2026, and how have Nasdaq's new IM-5101-4 delistings changed post-suspension price paths (the 2021-era literature on suspensions predates both)?

Has the ramp-and-dump pattern migrated after the 2026 Nasdaq rules to older listed microcaps or OTC names, as FINRA's 2025 report already hinted, and does the structural score need re-weighting away from listing age?
Is there any equity-market analogue of pre-pump target prediction (Xu & Livshits' 60% in crypto)? No equity study with out-of-sample returns was found.
What are the actual, out-of-sample win rates of Ortex and S3 squeeze signals? Neither vendor publishes squeeze-specific performance on its public pages.
